learning: Iteration 4 showed that narrowing wheel_track to 0.08 m lowered the score from 493.2 to 355.9 and raised s-bend oscillation to 0.45, so turn authority is not the slalom limit. Iteration 3 slalom still lost the line 0.35 times with max_error 0.0624. Iteration 1 showed loss near a 0.0565 m offset. This test checks whether +/-0.07 m reach removes the slalom line loss. If line loss stays at 0.3 or more, the next lever is controller kd or base_speed, not geometry.
notes: Iteration 3 geometry and controller, with the outer sensors widened from +/-0.06 to +/-0.07 m at about 23 mm spacing. The wheel track is restored to 0.10 m because iteration 4 showed that 0.08 m hurt every track. The controller is unchanged so the sensor-reach change is isolated.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (0.10 m track, 7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, lead 0.05 m, 0.6 kg, body 0.12 x 0.10 m, kd 0.6) scored 493.2, the best so far. Its s-bend line loss was 0 with progress 0.75, and the oval finish rate was 0.85. Iteration 4 narrowed the track to 0.08 m and scored 355.9. Oval, s-bend and slalom all got worse, and s-bend oscillation rose to 0.45, so turn authority is not the slalom limit and the 0.10 m track is restored. The slalom still lost the line 0.35 times per run with max_error 0.0624, just above the 0.06 m off-track floor. Body width cannot move that floor. Iteration 1 showed line loss at about 0.0565 m offset with a 72 mm span, so the outer sensors need more reach. This package keeps the iteration-3 controller unchanged (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.4, last_direction, proportional weights) and moves the outer sensors from x = +/-0.06 to +/-0.07 m, with about 23 mm spacing and 16 mm footprints. The sensor-reach change is therefore read alone against iteration 3. Expected: slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0 and slalom progress rises above 0.34. Risk: the wider span may add steering oscillation at edge crossings, so the oscillation figures are requested.
